st: In a bowl, mix the chicken with the yogurt, [[3 clove]] of the garlic, [[1.5 tsp]] of the ginger, [[1 tsp]] garam masala, the chili powder and a good pinch of salt.
Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 30 minutes, or up to overnight.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken in batches for about 4 minutes per batch until browned in spots. It does not need to be cooked through yet. Set aside.
In the same pan, melt [[2 tbsp]] of the butter over medium heat. Cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the remaining garlic and ginger and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes with [[1 tsp]] garam masala and the sugar. Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.
Blend the sauce with an immersion blender or in a regular blender until smooth, then return it to the pan.
Add the chicken and any juices, then simmer gently for 10 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) inside.
Stir in the cream, the remaining [[2 tbsp]] butter and the fenugreek leaves. Heat for 2 minutes without boiling hard.
Taste, add salt as needed, and serve with rice or naan.
Mix the chicken with the yogurt, garlic, ginger, [[2 tsp]] garam masala, turmeric, chili powder, half of the mint and cilantro, and [[2 tsp]] salt. Marinate for at least 1 hour.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] ghee in a pan over medium heat and fry the onions for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden brown. Set half aside for layering.
Add the marinated chicken and the other half of the onions to the pan and cook for 20 minutes, covered, until the chicken is tender and the sauce is thick.
Meanwhile, bring a large pot of water to a boil with [[2 tbsp]] salt, the cloves, cinnamon and cardamom.
Add the rice and boil for 5 minutes only, until about 70 percent cooked. Drain well.
Spread half of the rice over the chicken in the pan. Top with half the reserved onions, herbs and the remaining garam masala.
Add the rest of the rice, then the remaining onions and herbs. Drizzle with the saffron milk and the remaining [[2 tbsp]] ghee.
Cover with foil and a tight lid. Cook on the lowest heat for 25 minutes so the rice steams.
Turn off the heat and rest, covered, for 10 minutes. Make sure the chicken reads 165°F (74°C).
Gently fluff from the bottom up and serve with raita.
Heat the oil in a deep pan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes, stirring, until golden brown.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and green chili and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, coriander, turmeric and chili powder with [[1 tsp]] salt. Cook for 8 minutes, mashing the tomatoes, until the oil separates from the paste.
Add the chickpeas and the water. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat.
Simmer partly covered for 15 minutes. Mash a few chickpeas against the pan to thicken the gravy.
Stir in the garam masala and lemon juice. Taste and add salt if needed.
Top with cilantro and serve with rice, naan or bhatura.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add the spinach and cook for 2 minutes until wilted and bright green.
Drain the spinach and plunge it into cold water. Squeeze out the extra water and blend with the green chili into a coarse puree.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a skillet over medium heat. Fry the paneer cubes for 4 minutes, turning, until golden on a few sides. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, heat the remaining [[2 tbsp]] oil. Add the cumin seeds for 30 seconds, then the onion. Cook for 7 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 1 minute. Add the tomato, coriander and [[1 tsp]] salt and cook for 4 minutes until soft.
Pour in the spinach puree and stir well. Simmer on low for 6 minutes.
Stir in the cream and garam masala, then add the paneer. Warm gently for 3 minutes.
Taste, adjust salt, and serve with naan or rice.

ing: toor dal or split pigeon peas, rinsed
st: Put the lentils, water, turmeric and half of the tomato in a pot. Bring to a boil, then skim any foam.
Lower the heat, partly cover, and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils are very soft.
Mash the lentils lightly with a whisk or spoon. Stir in [[1 tsp]] salt and add a little hot water if too thick.
For the tadka, heat the ghee in a small pan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and wait until they sizzle.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until golden. Add the garlic and dried chilies and cook for 1 minute.
Add the rest of the tomato and the chili powder. Cook for 2 minutes until soft.
Pour the sizzling mixture over the dal and stir.
Finish with lemon juice and cilantro. Serve with rice or roti.
Mix the chicken with [[0.5 cup]] yogurt, half the garlic, half the ginger, [[1 tsp]] garam masala, the paprika, cumin, lemon juice and [[1 tsp]] salt. Marinate for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven broiler on high with a rack near the top. Thread chicken on skewers or lay on a lined tray.
Broil for 10 to 12 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges and 165°F (74°C) inside.
Meanwhile, heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 7 minutes until soft.
Add the remaining garlic and ginger and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomato puree, remaining [[1 tsp]] garam masala, the sugar and a pinch of salt. Simmer for 10 minutes until thick.
Stir in the remaining [[0.25 cup]] yogurt off the heat so it does not curdle, then add the cream.
Add the grilled chicken and simmer for 5 minutes. Add a splash of water if too thick.
Top with cilantro and serve with rice or naan.

ing: for the batter, plus more as needed
st: Soak the rice together with the fenugreek seeds in water for 6 hours. Soak the urad dal in a separate bowl for the same time.
Drain and grind the dal with [[0.5 cup]] of the water into a very fluffy batter. Grind the rice with the rest of the water until fine but slightly gritty.
Mix both batters with the [[1.5 tsp]] salt in a large bowl, cover loosely, and leave in a warm place for 8 to 10 hours until bubbly and sour-smelling.
For the filling, heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a pan. Add the mustard seeds until they pop, then the curry leaves, chili and ginger.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Stir in the turmeric and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Crumble in the potatoes, mix well with a splash of water, and cook for 3 minutes. Keep warm.
Heat a flat nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and wipe with a little oil. Thin the batter with water to the texture of heavy cream.
Pour a ladle of batter in the center and spread outward in a thin circle. Drizzle a little oil around the edge.
Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until deep golden and crisp. Spoon filling onto one half, fold over, and serve with chutney.

ing: for the dough, plus oil for frying
st: Mix the flour with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[4 tbsp]] oil. Add water a little at a time and knead for 5 minutes into a stiff dough. Rest, covered, for 30 minutes.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] of the frying oil in a pan. Add the cumin seeds, onion, chili and ginger and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the potatoes, peas, coriander, garam masala and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Mix well, cook for 3 minutes, and cool completely.
Divide the dough into 6 balls. Roll each into an oval, then cut in half to make 12 half circles.
Take one half circle, brush the straight edge with water, and fold into a cone, overlapping the edges.
Fill the cone with about [[2 tbsp]] of filling, brush the open rim with water, and press firmly to seal.
Heat the frying oil in a deep pot to 325°F (160°C). Fry the samosas in batches over medium-low heat.
Fry for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until deep golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels and serve warm with chutney.
Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm milk and leave for 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix the flour, salt and baking powder in a large bowl. Add the yeast milk, yogurt and oil.
Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and soft. Add a spoonful of flour only if it is very sticky.
Cover and let rise in a warm spot for 1 hour until doubled.
Mix the melted butter with the garlic and cilantro.
Divide the dough into 6 balls and roll each into a teardrop about 1/4 inch thick.
Heat a cast iron skillet over high heat until very hot. Cook one naan for 1 to 2 minutes until bubbles form, then flip.
Cook the second side for 1 to 2 minutes until charred in spots. Brush with garlic butter and keep wrapped in a towel while you cook the rest.
Mix the semolina, flour, baking soda and a pinch of salt. Add the warm water slowly and knead into a stiff dough. Cover with a damp cloth for 20 minutes.
Knead the dough again briefly and roll it very thin. Cut small circles about 1.5 inches wide with a cap or cutter.
Heat the frying oil to 375°F (190°C). Fry the circles a few at a time, pressing gently with a spoon so they puff into hollow balls.
Fry until golden and crisp, about 1 to 2 minutes, then drain on paper towels. Cool fully so they stay crisp.
Blend the mint, cilantro, chilies, ginger, tamarind paste, cumin and black salt with a little cold water into a smooth paste.
Stir the paste into the [[4 cup]] of cold water. Taste and add salt, then chill for 30 minutes.
Mix the potatoes, chickpeas, chaat masala and a pinch of salt for the filling.
To serve, crack a hole in the top of each puri, add a spoonful of filling, pour in the cold spiced water, and eat in one bite.
Boil the sugar, water and cardamom in a pot for 5 minutes until slightly sticky. Stir in the rose water and keep warm.
Mix the milk powder, flour and baking soda in a bowl. Add the ghee and rub it in with your fingers.
Add the warm milk a tablespoon at a time and mix gently into a soft dough. Do not knead hard or the balls will turn tough.
Rest the dough for 10 minutes. Rub a little ghee on your palms and roll into 12 smooth balls with no cracks.
Heat the frying oil over low heat to about 285°F (140°C). It must be gentle.
Fry the balls in small batches for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring the oil around them, until deep golden brown all over.
Drain briefly and drop into the warm syrup right away.
Soak for at least 30 minutes so they swell and absorb syrup. Serve warm or at room temperature.
Peel and dice the mango if you are using fresh fruit.
Put the mango, yogurt, milk and sugar into a blender.
Add the cardamom and the ice cubes.
Blend for 1 minute until completely smooth.
Taste and add more sugar if the mango is not very sweet.
Pour into two glasses and serve cold right away.
Mix flour, semolina, baking powder, sugar and salt in a bowl, then add yogurt and enough warm water to form a soft, slightly sticky dough.
Knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Coat with a little oil, cover and rest in a warm place for 2 hours.
Divide into 8 balls. Roll each into an oval about 6 inches long and thin enough that you can see your fingers through it.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 375°F, or until a pinch of dough rises right away.
Slide in one bhatura and press gently with a slotted spoon so it puffs up. Fry 30 seconds, flip and fry 30 seconds more until golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with chana masala.
nt: Deep fried at 375°F
Best swap: use cold-pressed non-dairy yogurt for a vegan dough; the puff will be a little lower.

st: Heat [[1 tbsp]] ghee in a wide heavy pot over medium heat. Fry the cashews and raisins for 1 minute until golden, then set aside.
Add the remaining [[2 tbsp]] ghee and the grated carrots. Saute for 8 minutes, stirring often, until the carrots soften and smell sweet.
Pour in the milk and bring to a boil. Reduce to medium-low and cook uncovered, stirring every few minutes, until the milk is almost fully absorbed, about 40 minutes.
Stir in [[0.75 cup]] sugar. The mixture will loosen, so cook 10 more minutes until it thickens again and the ghee separates at the edges.
Stir in the crushed cardamom seeds, fried cashews and raisins. Cook 2 minutes more.
Serve warm, topped with the sliced pistachios.
nt: Slow simmered in milk, stirred on the stovetop
Best swap: coconut oil for ghee and full-fat coconut milk for the milk, same amounts, for a dairy-free version.

st: Add [[1.5 cup]] water to a small saucepan with the crushed cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and [[1 tbsp]] grated ginger. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Lower the heat and simmer the spiced water for 2 minutes so the spices release their aroma and the water turns pale gold.
Stir in [[3 tsp]] loose tea and [[3 tbsp]] sugar. Simmer for 2 minutes until the liquid turns dark reddish brown.
Pour in [[1.5 cup]] whole milk and raise the heat to medium-high. Watch the pot, because the milk will rise fast.
When the foam climbs to the rim, lower the heat for a few seconds, then let it rise again. Repeat twice and simmer 3 minutes total until the chai is a creamy caramel color.
Strain through a fine sieve into cups, pressing the spices lightly. Serve right away, very hot.
nt: Simmered on the stovetop, tea boiled directly in the milk
Best swap: no CTC tea, use 2 Assam tea bags per cup of liquid; for dairy-free use oat milk at the same amount.

st: Cook the coconut and jaggery in a pan over low heat for 8 minutes, stirring, until the mix is sticky and no longer wet. Stir in cardamom, nutmeg and poppy seeds, then cool.
Bring the water, ghee and salt to a boil in a pot. Remove from heat and tip in the rice flour all at once. Stir, cover and rest 5 minutes.
Knead the hot dough with oiled hands for 3 minutes until smooth and crack-free. Cover with a damp cloth.
Press a golf ball size piece into a thin cup, pinching the rim into 5 to 6 pleats.
Add a tablespoon of filling and gather the pleats at the top, pinching them together to close in a point.
Place the modak on a greased steamer rack or banana leaf with space between them. Steam over boiling water for 12 minutes until glossy.
Serve warm with a spoon of ghee on top.
nt: Steamed over boiling water
Best swap: use brown sugar with 1 tsp molasses in place of jaggery, and desiccated coconut soaked in warm water for fresh coconut.

st: Bring the milk to a boil in a wide heavy pot over medium heat, stirring so it does not scorch on the bottom.
Lower the heat and simmer, scraping the sides back in, until the milk has reduced by about one third, about 30 minutes.
Stir in the condensed milk, [[2 tbsp]] sugar, the cream, cardamom and saffron. Simmer 5 more minutes until slightly thick, then add half the pistachios.
Cool the mixture completely to room temperature, stirring now and then so no skin forms.
Pour into kulfi molds, small cups or a loaf pan and cover with foil. Freeze for at least 6 hours until solid.
Dip the mold in warm water for 10 seconds, unmold, slice and top with the remaining pistachios.
nt: Slow-simmered, then frozen
Best swap: use a 13.5 oz can of full-fat evaporated milk in place of the reduced milk for a 15 minute shortcut.

st: Wash the apples, guava and grapes in cold water, scrubbing the apple skin, then dry them. Halve the grapes and peel and segment the oranges, removing any membrane and seeds.
Cut the apples and guava into 2 cm cubes, discarding the apple core and seeds. Squeeze the lime over them straight away so they do not brown.
Add the pomegranate arils, orange segments and grapes to a large bowl, and toss with the apple and guava.
Slice the bananas into thick rounds only just before serving, since they soften fast. Fold them in lightly.
Sprinkle [[1 tsp]] chaat masala, [[0.5 tsp]] black salt and [[0.5 tsp]] roasted cumin over the fruit. Add the mint and toss softly with a spoon.
Taste and adjust: add more lime if you want it tarter, or a pinch more black salt if it needs to be sharper.
Serve right away in small bowls or leaf cups, with toothpicks. Do not let it sit, or the salt will pull water from the fruit.
nt: No cook: cut and toss with spices
Best swap: regular salt plus a pinch of ground cumin for black salt, and ripe pear for guava if guava is not available.

ing: skin removed, slashed to the bone
st: Cut deep slashes to the bone in each piece. Rub with [[3 tbsp]] lemon juice and [[1 tsp]] salt and rest 20 minutes so the first marinade can penetrate.
Whisk the yogurt with the ginger garlic paste, [[1.5 tbsp]] chili powder, [[2 tsp]] garam masala, cumin, fenugreek and [[2 tbsp]] oil until smooth.
Coat the chicken thoroughly in the yogurt mixture, working it into the slashes. Cover and marinate in the fridge at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Heat the oven to 475°F with a rack in the upper third. Place chicken on a wire rack set over a foil lined tray so heat circulates all around.
Roast 20 minutes, flip, then roast 15 to 20 minutes more until charred in spots and 175°F in the thickest thigh. Switch to broil for the last 3 minutes for blackened edges.
Rest 5 minutes. Squeeze lemon over and serve with sliced onion, mint chutney and naan.
nt: Roasted at very high heat to mimic a clay tandoor, then charred under the broiler
Best swap: grill over hot coals 6 minutes per side. Use 1 tsp paprika plus a pinch of cayenne in place of Kashmiri chili powder.

st: Squeeze the lemons into a pitcher, removing any seeds. You want about [[0.5 cup]] juice.
Add [[3 tbsp]] sugar and [[2 cups]] cold water, stirring until the sugar fully dissolves.
Stir in the black salt and roasted cumin, then add the remaining cold water.
Taste and adjust: it should be tangy, lightly sweet and a little savory.
Add torn mint and plenty of ice. Serve right away.
nt: No cook: squeeze, stir and chill
Best swap: no black salt, use 0.5 tsp regular salt plus a pinch of chaat masala; swap sugar with the same amount of honey.

st: Soak the beans in plenty of water overnight. Drain and rinse.
Boil the beans in fresh water with [[1 tsp]] salt for 45 minutes at a steady simmer (or use a pressure cooker for 20 minutes) until soft enough to mash easily. Keep the cooking water.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add the onions and cook for 10 minutes, stirring, until deep golden brown.
Stir in the ginger and garlic for 1 minute, then add the tomato puree, [[2 tsp]] coriander, chili powder and turmeric. Cook until oil separates at the edges, about 8 minutes.
Add the beans with [[2 cups]] of their cooking water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Mash a few beans against the pot side to thicken. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in the garam masala and cilantro. Serve with steamed rice.
nt: Boiled, then simmered
Best swap: canned kidney beans work, use three 15 oz cans drained and simmer only 15 minutes.

ing: finely minced, seeded for less heat
st: Peel the cucumbers if the skin is thick, then cut into 1/2 inch cubes and place in a large bowl.
Dice the tomatoes to the same size, discarding the watery seeds if they are very juicy, and add to the bowl.
Dice the red onion into small pieces and add it along with the minced green chili and cilantro.
Sprinkle in [[0.5 tsp]] cumin powder, [[0.5 tsp]] chaat masala and salt. Pour in [[2 tbsp]] lemon juice.
Toss well and serve within 20 minutes while the vegetables are still crisp. Serve with biryani, dal or grilled meats.
nt: No cook: chopped and tossed
Best swap: skip the chaat masala and use a pinch of ground coriander plus extra lemon juice.

st: Stir [[1 tbsp]] sabja seeds into [[0.5 cup]] water and let sit for 15 minutes until they swell and form a clear jelly coat.
Boil the falooda sev in water for 3 to 4 minutes until soft, then drain and rinse under cold water. Set aside.
Whisk the cold milk with [[2 tbsp]] rose syrup until evenly pink.
Into each tall glass, spoon [[2 tbsp]] rose syrup in total, then half the soaked seeds and half the noodles.
Pour in the rose milk slowly, then top each glass with a scoop of ice cream.
Sprinkle with pistachios and serve with a long spoon and a straw.
nt: Boiled noodles, then assembled cold
Best swap: use cooked rice noodles or cornstarch vermicelli for falooda sev, and chia seeds for sabja.

st: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot for 6 minutes until the onion is soft and golden at the edges.
Add the garlic, ginger and [[1.5 tbsp]] curry powder. Stir for 1 minute until fragrant so the spices toast but do not burn.
Add the chicken and stir for 3 minutes to coat it in the spices. Pour in the stock and add the lentils and salt.
Bring to a boil, then lower to a simmer, partly covered, for 25 minutes until the lentils are soft and the chicken reaches 165°F inside.
Lift out the chicken, shred it with two forks, and return it to the pot. Blend a third of the soup with an immersion blender for body.
Stir in the coconut milk and warm for 3 minutes without boiling hard. Finish with the lemon juice and adjust salt.
nt: Sauteed aromatics, then simmered
Best swap: chickpeas or diced sweet potato instead of chicken for a vegetarian version, with vegetable stock.

st: If your samosas are cold, warm them in a 375°F oven for 8 minutes until crisp and hot all the way through.
Warm the chickpeas in a small pot over medium heat with the cumin powder and a splash of water for 3 minutes. Mash a few so the mixture turns thick.
Break each samosa into big chunks in a shallow bowl, crushing it roughly with the back of a spoon.
Spoon the warm chickpeas over the samosa, then pour on the whisked yogurt.
Drizzle with the tamarind and green chutneys, then scatter the onion, tomato, chaat masala and cilantro on top.
Finish with the sev and serve immediately so the samosa pieces stay a little crisp.
nt: Reheated samosa topped with cold and warm toppings, no frying
Best swap: use dairy-free yogurt for a vegan plate, or crushed potato chips if you cannot find sev.
